overview: Start with a modular monolith, route-level code splitting and explicit feature exports. The shell owns navigation/session/error boundaries; feature modules own their state and APIs. SSR public discovery routes selectively and CSR authenticated tools when appropriate. Adopt independently deployed microfrontends only for concrete team/deploy constraints. The graph separates browser interaction state, server query state and the existing backend. It is one defensible approach; equivalent boundaries and well-argued alternatives are welcome.
limitations: Design checks inspect structure and written evidence only; they do not execute a UI or prove accessibility/performance.

estimation.result: Set production bundle budgets and analyze duplicate dependencies
estimation.implication: Measure cache-cold vs warm navigation and hydration; compression changes transfer size.

components.purpose: Start with a modular monolith, route-level code splitting and explicit feature exports. The shell owns navigation/session/error boundaries; feature modules own their state and APIs. SSR public discovery routes selectively and CSR authenticated tools when appropriate. Adopt independently deployed microfrontends only for concrete team/deploy constraints. Performance plan: 3 large feature areas; initial load should include shell + active route, not all feature code; track real-user route failures. Accessibility: Provide skip links, route heading/focus management, document-title updates and keyboard navigation. Route errors must expose recovery without losing shell controls. Failure recovery: Use a guarded refresh prompt for chunk-version failure; cancel old-tenant requests and clear caches before rendering new data. Add route-level error boundaries and release-correlated monitoring. Trade-off: Microfrontends enable independent release ownership but add shared-runtime, CSS, routing and observability costs. A modular monolith is sufficient until organizational constraints justify these costs.

failureCases.scenario: Route or identity changes while work is in flight
failureCases.handling: Dispose subscriptions, abort obsolete reads and ignore old generations; partition/clear private cache before showing a new account. Preserve only explicitly safe drafts.
